summary: notification-service is being OOMKilled by unbounded heap growth from the new in-memory TemplateCache introduced in dep-5402 (v3.8.0, deployed 2026-03-21T00:00Z). Memory_pct climbs monotonically from ~47% to ~98% over ~22h and then resets, repeating daily on 03-21, 03-22 and 03-23 — a daily restart cadence matching the cumulative restarts counter (1, 2, 3) and the 03-23T19:59:21Z OOMKilled (exit 137) log. TemplateCache logs confirm the map grows to 196,650 entries with 0 evictions. CPU (~25%) and latency (~110ms) are flat; Kafka is healthy (cpu ~35%, ~2300 msg/s). The consumer_lag spike (~18k) occurs only after the 19:59 restart (and similarly after the 03-22 restart), consistent with post-restart replay, not a cause. The 03-23 18:00 Kafka retention change (cfg-2410) is a red herring: OOMs predate it and no throughput surge accompanied it. Recommended fix: roll back dep-5402 or add a bounded cache with eviction/size cap.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unbounded TemplateCache (dep-5402) causes gradual heap growth and OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0, 03-21) introduced an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap template cache with no eviction bound. Heap grows monotonically at render traffic until the container exceeds its memory limit and is OOMKilled (~daily), producing the repeated restarts and delayed emails. The post-restart consumer lag spike is the replay backlog draining, not the trigger.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 deploys unbounded in-memory template cache on render path
Container exceeds memory limit -> OOMKilled restart
During restart, consumer group re-reads/replays -> lag spike and delayed emails

assumptions: The rendered-template cardinality (template+locale+userSegment) is effectively unbounded so the map never stops growing
The leaked TemplateCache lives in the same heap measured by memory_pct
Heap plateau at ~98% then reset corresponds to the OOM restart rather than a GC reclaim

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance/replay causes consumer to choke and OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The 03-23 18:00 Kafka retention change (cfg-2410) and/or broker maintenance triggered a consumer replay storm; the consumer re-fetched a large backlog, the in-memory processing buffer grew, and the container was OOMKilled at 19:59. This is the on-call's stated hypothesis.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2410 reduces Kafka retention at 18:00 on 03-23
Replay backlog is re-consumed by notification-service
Buffer growth during replay drives OOM

assumptions: Retention reduction would actually force a re-fetch (retention changes typically delete old segments, not force replay)
OOMs on 03-21 and 03-22 were caused by the same mechanism

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load/throughput growth (capacity saturation)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Notification render traffic outgrew the provisioned memory, causing OOM.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: CPU flat ~25%, Kafka messages/s flat ~2300, latency flat — no load surge; memory grows as a bounded sawtooth independent of traffic.

facts.statement: notification-service memory follows a daily sawtooth rising from ~47% to ~98% then resetting to ~49% on each of 03-21, 03-22 and 03-23.
TemplateCache grows unbounded with evictions=0, reaching 196,650 entries.
dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 03-21T00:00Z) added the TemplateCache on the render path and remains live.
An OOMKilled restart (exit 137) occurred at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z after heap-over-threshold GC warnings from 18:34:46Z.
Cumulative restarts rose 1 (03-21) -> 2 (03-22) -> 3 (03-23), one per day.
CPU (~25%) and latency_p99 (~110ms) were flat on 03-23; Kafka CPU (~35%) and messages_in_per_s (~2300) were flat.
consumer_lag spiked to ~18k only after the 19:59 restart on 03-23 (and after the ~21:00 restart on 03-22), vs baseline ~50-70.
The only config change was the 03-23 18:00 Kafka retention reduction (cfg-2410); nothing changed on notification-service.
notification-service depends on Kafka (consume) and an external email-provider.
The daily OOM pattern began 03-21, preceding the 03-23 Kafka maintenance by two days.

assumptions: The leaked TemplateCache resides in the same heap measured by memory_pct (no separate native/off-heap accounting).
The memory plateau-then-reset at ~98% corresponds to the OOMKilled restart, and the daily reset period equals the observed restart cadence.
Rendered-template key cardinality (template+locale+userSegment) is effectively unbounded so the cache never stops growing.

timeline.event: dep-5402 v3.8.0 deployed to notification-service adding in-memory TemplateCache
First OOM restart (restart count -> 1); memory had climbed to ~97%
Second OOM restart (restart count -> 2) with same memory sawtooth
Heap-over-90% old-gen GC warnings begin on notification-service
consumer_lag spikes to ~18k as post-restart backlog replays; emails delayed ~25 min

recommended_actions.action: Roll back / disable dep-5402 (TemplateCache) on notification-service, or set a bounded cache (max size + eviction, e.g. Caffeine with maximumSize/TTL).
recommended_actions.rationale: Cache is the leak source: unbounded growth with evictions=0 matching the daily OOM cadence.

recommended_actions.action: Raise the container memory limit only as a temporary buffer and/or alert on memory_pct slope, not just threshold.
recommended_actions.rationale: Buys time while the leak fix ships; a slope alert catches the ramp before OOM.

recommended_actions.action: Add a cache-size/eviction metric and a unit test asserting the cache is bounded under high-cardinality keys.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents recurrence of unbounded in-memory caches on the render path.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT act on the Kafka maintenance as the cause; keep a post-restart replay drain watch instead.
recommended_actions.rationale: Lag spike is a downstream consequence of the restart, and OOMs predate the config change.

data_gaps: No heap dump / per-component memory breakdown to prove TemplateCache is the exact allocation dominating the heap (inferred from size growth + evictions=0 + timing).

Kafka consumer_lag metric is not exposed on the kafka service itself (only cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions), so partition-reassignment activity cannot be directly confirmed or excluded.
email-provider has no telemetry, so its contribution to delayed emails cannot be measured.
No data before 2026-03-21, so it is not directly verifiable that no OOM occurred prior to dep-5402.

findings.statement: notification-service memory_pct shows a daily sawtooth: monotonic growth from ~47% to ~98% over ~22h followed by a reset to ~49%, repeating on 03-21, 03-22 and 03-23.
TemplateCache grows unbounded with zero evictions: size climbs 49500 -> 99000 -> 148500 (03-23) and reached 196650 entries with evictions=0 on 03-21/03-22.

Deployment dep-5402 (notification-service v3.8.0, deployed 2026-03-21T00:00:00Z) added an in-memory template cache 'TemplateCache (ConcurrentHashMap) keyed by template+locale+userSegment' on the render path; it is live and not rolled back.

findings.statement: notification-service experienced OOMKilled restarts: log shows 'container notification-service-7d9f OOMKilled (exit code 137), restarting' at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z, preceded by heap-over-threshold/full GC warnings starting 2026-03-23T18:34:46Z.

refs.quote: heap usage 5% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4152ms

findings.statement: Cumulative restart count for notification-service rose to 1 around 03-21 21:00-24:00, to 2 around 03-22 21:00, and to 3 around 03-23 18:00-21:00.
notification-service CPU is flat ~25% and latency_p99 is flat ~110ms throughout 03-23, with no surge coincident with the OOM.
Kafka is healthy on 03-23: cpu_pct flat ~35% and messages_in_per_s steady ~2300 with max 2532.9, no throughput surge.

consumer_lag for notification-service spiked to avg ~3000 / max ~18000 only in the 19:30-21:00 bucket on 03-23 (after the 19:59 restart), and similarly at the ~21:00 bucket on 03-22; baseline lag is ~50-70.

The only config change was cfg-2410 on service 'kafka', log.retention.ms reduced to 259200000 at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z ('Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days'); no config change on notification-service.

refs.quote: Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days

findings.statement: notification-service depends on kafka (queue-consume) and email-provider (external); kafka is shared and has telemetry, email-provider has no telemetry.

The first OOM period (memory sawtooth restart) began on 03-21, before the 03-23 Kafka maintenance; GC/memory pressure warnings on 03-23 start at 18:34, i.e., only ~34 min after the 18:00 Kafka change but part of a pattern already present for two days.
Historical incidents with similar 'consumer lag spike / delayed emails' symptoms cite Kafka partition reassignment/rebalance (HIST-104, HIST-112) as root cause.
